title: Furniture and shop layout
summary: Furniture in Supermarket Simulator arrives as a box you have to handle: you buy a piece, take it out of the box in a placing mode, and the game shows you where that piece is allowed to stand.
body: Furniture is bought as a box. A piece arrives packed and has to be handled before it can be used, which is why an empty shop ends up with furniture boxes sitting around after a delivery rather than a finished aisle.
Putting it down is its own mode. The game switches you into a placing mode for the box and a placing mode for the piece, so you are never simply dropping furniture wherever you happen to be standing.
The game decides where a piece is allowed to go. Furniture carries snap points and a snap direction, so a unit locks onto a sensible position instead of floating wherever the camera was pointing.

The range on offer is data, not a fixed counter. What you can buy is listed through the game's own furniture records, and a layout setting governs how the shop is arranged, which is why the catalogue can differ from one shop to the next.

Furniture can be taken back out as well. There is an interface for things the game is allowed to remove and a manager that handles those removals, which is why rearranging a shop is a supported job rather than a one-way purchase.

Putting it down is a job of its own. The build keeps a placer for furniture and a way to handle its boxes in a batch, which is why a delivery of fittings can be dealt with as a set rather than one crate at a time.
What this entry does not tell you: prices, how many pieces exist, or which furniture earns the most. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.

facts.claim: Furniture arrives in a box that has to be handled before the piece can be used.
Placing a piece is a separate mode from carrying its box.
The game defines snap points and a snap direction that decide where a piece may sit.
Furniture is offered and presented through the game's own furniture records.
The furniture options come from one layout setting.
Furniture can be removed as well as placed: there is an interface for things that can be destroyed and a manager that handles them.
The build keeps a placer for furniture and a way to batch the boxes it arrives in.
The build names an advertising pillar and a point-of-sale terminal among the fixtures a shop can hold.
The build also names a fountain element of its own among the things a shop can hold.
Mirrors are held as objects of their own with a collider beside them.
A magazine rack is named among the fittings a shop can hold.

The build names its shelves by shape and by colour: concave and convex shelves in dune, gulf stream, jungle mist, lunar green, pale orange, pine glade, rock blue, sandrift, ship gray, sprout, terracotta and viola.
facts.evidence: asset names: Concave_Shelf_Dune, Concave_Shelf_Terracotta, Concave_Shelf_Viola, Convex_Shelf_Lunar Green, Convex_Shelf_Rock Blue, Convex_Shelf_London Hue
